title: Diagnostic
description: One structured finding (LSP-shaped) carried in a result envelope's `diagnostics` array (CLI-SPEC §4). Built to be corrective — detect → locate → repair: a stable `code`, a `where`, and (for recoverable errors) a `fix`.

severity.description: ERROR = blocks the result (the envelope's outcome is refused [exit 2] or rejected [exit 1]; nothing written); WARNING = valid-but-suspicious advisory (outcome stays applied/read, exit 0); INFO = a note (e.g. a version skew), exit 0. Rule of thumb: an ERROR-severity diagnostic explains a non-zero exit; WARNING/INFO ride a successful one.

source.description: KERNEL = the kernel refused: checkConsistency may report named or codeless notifications; deserialize/expand may refuse before judgment; or checkConsistency may throw while building the model, in which case the codeless summary begins `the kernel could not build this model:`. Code absence alone does not identify the tier. PRECHECK = a kit pre-check, including malformed model input (RK_MODEL_INPUT_INVALID, exit 2, with no consistency verdict); LINT = valid-but-suspicious advisory; ENVIRONMENT = toolchain note; INTERNAL = an unexpected tool failure.

code.description: Stable identifier when present. KERNEL notifications can be codeless even after checkConsistency judges the model; code absence also occurs on deserialization and model-build refusals. An MVK_* code alone does not attribute the decision: typed builders also emit these codes at source PRECHECK. Use source to identify the producer and the build-failure summary to distinguish a failed model build. Look up RK_* codes and structural MVK_* correctives with `dmtool diagnostics <CODE>`; operator-specific MVK_* codes are explained by `operators`/`explain`.

where.description: the locus — a rule-condition site (rule/operator/span) OR a structure site (path/arg)

path.description: a model-element path (structure locus — modelkit ops)

span.description: [start, end] char offsets into the condition text, when known

fix.description: the actionable repair — an applicable replacement or a discovery command; present for recoverable errors

explain.description: the operator meaning / rationale (the `why`), when helpful

examples.summary: The error code is only allowed to contain letters, digits, blanks and underscores.
'/Order/Quantity' is a number compared with an ordering operator but its presence isn't guarded
examples.explain: an unspecified number defaults to 0 in a comparison (KERNEL-SEMANTICS §2)

examples.summary: /Order/DeliveryDate is referenced by 1 element(s); removing it would dangle them
examples.fix: pass --cascade to remove the referrers too, or remove them first
